sources.excerpt: most common clinical manifestations of an allergic reaction to a food or food additive. Symptoms range from acute urticaria (most common) to flushing to angioedema to exacerbations of atopic dermatitis. Food allergy is rarely the cause of chronic urticaria or angioedema. Atopic dermatitis Controversy surrounds the role of food allergy in the pathogenesis of atopic dermatitis. Studies show that among patients with moderate chronic atopic dermatitis, 35-40% have IgE-mediated food allergy. Food-specific IgE-mediated and cellular mechanisms appear responsible for chronic eczematous inflammation.

diseases.name: Lyme disease
diseases.rationale: The questionnaire asks about the source of the bite, which could be a tick. Lyme disease is a tick-borne illness that can present with an expanding rash (erythema migrans) at the bite site, along with non-specific symptoms like fatigue, myalgias, headache, fever, and chills, which are covered in the systemic symptoms question.

diseases.name: Tick-borne rickettsial disease
diseases.rationale: The questionnaire asks about the source of the bite. If a tick is identified, rickettsial diseases are a key consideration. The provided evidence discusses the diagnosis and management of these diseases, which can be associated with tick bites.

diseases.name: Alpha-gal syndrome
diseases.rationale: This condition is associated with bites from the lone star tick. It can cause a delayed allergic reaction, including urticaria, angioedema, and anaphylaxis, 4-6 hours after consuming mammalian meat. The questionnaire asks about systemic symptoms like hives, itching, and swelling of the face, lips, or tongue, which are consistent with this syndrome.

diseases.name: Wound infection
diseases.rationale: The questionnaire asks about local symptoms like worsening redness, swelling, and systemic symptoms like fever. These are classic signs of a wound infection, which is a common complication of any bite, including human bites.

diseases.name: Allergic reaction
diseases.rationale: The questionnaire asks about initial reactions like swelling and redness, as well as systemic symptoms like hives (urticaria), itching, swelling of the face/lips/tongue, and difficulty breathing. These are hallmark symptoms of an allergic reaction, which can be triggered by an insect or animal bite.
